newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian Nika says 1996 net down 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian Nika says 1996 net down 11 pct.

text.p: Slovenian brokerage Nika said on Thursday 1996 net profit fell to 81 million tolars ($514,285) from 91 million a year earlier as the Ljubljana bourse's performance deteriorated.

"Nika is investing mostly on the Ljubljana bourse, so our profit depends largely on the performance of the blue-chip index and the shares in our portfolio, which was not the best last year," general manager Branko Susteric told Reuters.
Slovenia's blue-chip SBI index fell 14.9 percent over the course of the year.
Nika plans to pay a 1996 dividend of 180 tolars per share, down from 200 tolars a year earlier.
Susteric said the company's balance sheet assets rose to 2.6 billion tolars in 1996 from 2.3 billion a year ago and added he expected assets to rise to about three billion tolars this year.
He said net profit was expected to exceed 100 million tolars this year.
